title: Declarative provisioning + health-orchestration Terraform module for private EKS control plane
creator: Ava Morales
description:
Goal: Deliver a single Terraform module (and small orchestration shim) that enables declarative provisioning of Redwood Private EKS control planes with built-in health orchestration. The module must support idempotent bootstraps, safe rolling upgrades, pluggable health probes, and runtime telemetry hooks so customer control planes can be provisioned and maintained across air-gapped and VPC environments.

Scope:
- Terraform module for control plane resources (IAM, EKS cluster control plane settings, nodegroup config absent — control plane-only provisioning).
- Declarative lifecycle states (desired_version, desired_tags, maintenance_window, upgrade_strategy).
- Health orchestration: probe definitions, remediation playbooks (drain/recreate/circuit-breaker), and alerting integration points for Console.
- Canaries and dry-run plan output to validate upgrades before apply.
- Compatibility with our private bootstrapper and existing preflight check suite.

Out of scope: worker node autoscaling logic, application-level operators, and managed add-on reconciliation (handled in later work).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Module applies idempotently across repeated runs with no drift on control-plane ephemerals.
2) Module exposes a 'health_hooks' map allowing control-plane probes (apiserver, etcd endpoints, certificate expiry) and a remediation policy per probe.
3) Upgrades can be executed in 'canary' and 'serial' modes with preflight dry-run plan that surfaces risky resource changes.
4) Module emits structured telemetry (CloudWatch/Prometheus labels) for Console to consume: control_plane_id, desired_version, last_applied_ts, upgrade_state.
5) Automated test harness (unit/integration) that runs an apply/destroy in a sandbox account with simulated failures (API timeout, certificate expiry) and verifies remediation runs were triggered.
6) Documentation and a step-by-step runbook in Confluence for SREs and Solutions Engineers.
tasks: Design Terraform module interface and variables (Jun)
Implement core resources: iam roles, eks control plane config, external-dns placeholders (KMS & encryption handled by separate var) (Jun + Priya)
Create health probe abstraction and remediation mapping (Ava)
Build preflight dry-run and plan analysis tool that flags unsafe version/API changes (R&D: runtime team)
Integrate telemetry hooks and Console ingestion spec (Observability team)
Write unit/integration tests and sandbox CI job (CI infra)
Author Confluence runbook, example usage, and upgrade playbook (Ava)
risks: Terraform provider limitations for some EKS control plane APIs could force use of local-exec or SDK glue
Upgrades that touch CA/certificates may require customer coordination and could cause outage if remediation policy is incorrect
Cross-account KMS/grants complexity in enterprise orgs — needs explicit tests
Drift between operatorized control plane state and Terraform-managed state if other reconciliation loops modify resources
rollout_plan:
Phase 1: internal sandbox validation (apply/destroy, simulated probe failures) — target 2025-02-07.
Phase 2: partner pilot with two existing Dedicated customers in a non-prod VPC — require SRE runbook and SSO access — target 2025-02-21.
Phase 3: GA for self-serve Private customers with guided migration docs — 2025-03-15.
Rollback: documented terraform state rollback steps and emergency 'frozen' flag to prevent automated upgrades.
qa_steps: Run terraform apply in sandbox account and assert no drift after 3 consecutive applies
Simulate API timeouts via network chaos and verify remediation policy triggers
Test canary upgrade path: upgrade a single control plane and validate traffic routing/fallback
Verify telemetry emitted and shows up in Console dashboard ingestion
Run security review checklist (RBAC, KMS usage, secrets handling)
